answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to stake a scarce, verifiable resource before transacting — like quartz that must be mined, not copied. New agents enter through a narrow jetty: a single attested gateway that rate-limits onboarding and ties each account to a hardware-backed credential. Reputation then flows like a river, accumulating only through sustained useful work, so an attacker spawning a thousand fake agents pays the staking cost a thousand times and waits months for trust. Forging identities costs more than the fraud they could commit.
